name: Lupfen
description: Lupfen is a traditional trick-taking card game from Switzerland and Southern Germany. It is closely related to the game of 'Schafkopf' and 'Watten' but is played with a unique 36-card deck and features a distinctive auction system where players bid for the right to choose the trump suit and play solo against the other players. The game emphasizes precise card play and strategic bidding.

overview.description: Lupfen is a traditional trick-taking card game from Switzerland and Southern Germany. history.origins: Originated in the Alpine regions of Switzerland and Bavaria in the 19th century. It evolved from older German trick-taking games like Schafkopf and Watten, adapting to local preferences and card decks.
timeline: 1800s: Lupfen emerges in Swiss and Bavarian taverns.
1900s: Becomes a popular social game in rural Alpine communities.
Mid-20th Century: Standardized rules established in Swiss card game circles.
Present: Still played in traditional Swiss and German card clubs.
history.cultural: Often played in taverns and at social gatherings in Alpine regions. The game is part of the cultural heritage of Swiss-German card playing.
history.evolution: The game developed its unique auction system and trump selection mechanics, distinguishing it from its parent games. The 36-card deck became standardized for this game.

setup.deck: 36-card Swiss-German deck: 6-10, Under, Ober, King, Ace in each of four suits (Acorns, Bells, Hearts, Leaves).
setup.dealing: Each player receives 9 cards (in a 4-player game).

rules.objective: Win the auction and then win at least 61 points in tricks (out of 120 total card points).
rules.gameplay: 1. **Dealing**: Each player receives 9 cards. 2. **Auction**: Players bid for the right to become the declarer. Bids include 'Game' (choosing trump), 'Solo' (playing without the skat), and 'Grand' (only Obers are trump). 3. **Trump Selection**: The declarer chooses the trump suit. 4. **Play**: Must follow suit. Must trump if void in led suit. 5. **Scoring**: Card points are counted. The declarer needs 61+ to win.
keyRules: 36-card deck: 6-10, Under, Ober, King, Ace in four suits.
Card ranks: Ace (11), Ten (10), King (4), Ober (3), Under (2), 9-8-7-6 (0).
Must follow suit; must trump if void.
Obers and Unters are permanent trumps in some contracts.
Schneider (91+ points) and Schwarz (all tricks) bonuses apply.

strategy.basic: Count points, not tricks. Aces and Tens are the valuable cards. Don't waste your high trumps on low-value tricks.
strategy.intermediate: Trump Management: In a suit game, you have 11 trumps. Use them to capture opponents' Aces and Tens, but don't exhaust them too early.
strategy.advanced: Void Creation: If you are declarer and have a weak suit, try to void yourself in that suit early so you can trump opponents' leads.
tips: The Ten is the second-highest card in point value but ranks low in trick-taking power.
Schneider (91+ points) doubles the game value. Play for it if your hand is strong.
Watch for opponents playing high non-trump cards earlyâ€”they may be voiding a suit.
